question: Cross-domain: Can tumor-derived exosome proteomics predict organ-specific metastasis tropism via a multi-modal ML model trained on spatial transcriptomics?
verdict: Exosomal integrin/proteome profiles combined with HTAN spatial immune-stroma features predict which organ a tumor will metastasize to, enabling pre-metastatic niche interception.
citableArgument: Merge exosome protein mass-spec (EV-TRACK) with HTAN spatial transcriptomics (21 sites) and clinical metastasis annotation (SEER). Train a multi-modal classifier with cross-validation.
plainLanguageVerdict: By combining what tumors release in exosomes with where cells sit in the tissue, we can predict which organ the cancer will spread to next.

subExperiments.title: Exosome protein feature extraction (mass spec → embeddings)
Spatial feature extraction from HTAN (immune neighborhoods)

ethicalNotes: De-identified exosome/proteome data; HTAN data-use policies; FDA guidance on biomarker development.

question: Cross-domain: Does a CRISPR base-editing perturbation screen in paired primary/metastatic isogenic lines reveal synthetic-lethal vulnerabilities that are invisible in single-site screens?
verdict: Base-editing perturbation screens in matched primary-metastasis cell pairs identify site-specific vulnerabilities (e.g., metastasis-specific dependencies on chromatin remodelers) not visible in single-site screens.
citableArgument: Generate matched primary/metastatic cell lines from patient-derived xenografts. Run genome-wide base-editor screens (Nature Biotech 2026 approach) in both. Compare dependency scores.
ethicalNotes: PDX work requires IACUC; CRISPR safety review; patient tissue consent.

question: Cross-domain: Can single-cell Perturb-seq of tumor-infiltrating T cells identify which genetic perturbations reverse exhaustion and synergize with checkpoint blockade?
verdict: Perturb-seq in tumor-infiltrating T cells reveals genetic edits (e.g., TOX, NR4A family knockdowns) that reverse exhaustion and synergize with anti-PD-1 therapy.
citableArgument: Use Perturb-CITE-seq (Broad 2025) in syngeneic tumor models to map perturbation → T-cell state. Identify edits that improve checkpoint blockade response.

subExperiments.title: In vivo screen in syngeneic tumor model
Single-cell state analysis + exhaustion reversal scoring

ethicalNotes: IACUC for syngeneic models; FDA IND for any clinical translation.

question: Cross-domain: Can a deep-learning model on pre-treatment MRI + liquid biopsy (ctDNA + exosomes) predict which glioblastoma patients will respond to EGFR+PARP combination therapy?
anchorLabel: MRI + ctDNA + exosome → GBM combo response (XD-04)
verdict: Multi-modal fusion (MRI radiomics + CSF ctDNA + exosome proteome) predicts GBM response to EGFR+PARP combo better than any single modality.
citableArgument: Combine BraTS MRI, CSF ctDNA (ultra-deep NGS), and exosome protein panels. Train multi-modal classifier. Validate on Phase I cohort.

subExperiments.title: ctDNA mutation calling from CSF (ultra-deep NGS)

ethicalNotes: Pediatric/adult GBM consent; FDA IND; IRB for CSF collection.

question: Cross-domain: Can spatial multi-omics of paired primary/metastatic lesions reveal immune-exclusion mechanisms that predict checkpoint-inhibitor failure in metastatic disease?
anchorLabel: Spatial omics × paired primary/met × checkpoint failure (XD-05)
verdict: Spatial transcriptomics + multiplex IHC of paired primary/metastatic lesions reveals immune-exclusion neighborhoods that predict checkpoint-inhibitor failure.
citableArgument: HTAN spatial data + paired biopsy banks. Compare immune neighborhoods (T-cell exclusion, myeloid suppression) between primary and metastatic. Correlate with checkpoint response.
ethicalNotes: Paired biopsy consent; de-identification of spatial metadata.

question: Cross-domain: Can an exosome-based liquid biopsy signature distinguish tumor recurrence from radiation necrosis in post-treatment glioma, replacing invasive re-biopsy?
anchorLabel: Exosome liquid biopsy × recurrence vs necrosis (XD-06)
verdict: Exosomal miRNA/protein signatures in plasma distinguish tumor recurrence from radiation necrosis with AUC≥0.85, potentially replacing invasive re-biopsy.
citableArgument: Collect plasma exosomes from post-treatment glioma patients with confirmed recurrence vs necrosis (pathology). Train classifier on exosomal miRNA + protein panel.
ethicalNotes: IRB for plasma collection; HIPAA; FDA device review if clinical use.

question: Cross-domain: Can a federated learning model across 5 hospitals predict pediatric brain tumor molecular subtypes from MRI without sharing patient data?
anchorLabel: Federated learning × pediatric brain MRI × molecular subtype (XD-07)
verdict: Federated learning across 5 institutions achieves ≥85% accuracy for IDH/medulloblastoma subtype classification from MRI without centralizing patient data.
citableArgument: Deploy federated MRI radiomics model across 5 hospitals. Each site trains locally, shares model weights. Aggregate via FedAvg. Validate on held-out institutional data.

subExperiments.title: Local radiomic feature extraction per site

ethicalNotes: HIPAA/GDPR compliance; federated learning ethics review; parental consent for pediatric MRI.

question: Cross-domain: Can tumor mutation burden (TMB) + microbiome composition predict immunotherapy response better than TMB alone in lung cancer?
verdict: Gut microbiome diversity + TMB combined signature predicts checkpoint inhibitor response with higher AUC than TMB alone in NSCLC.
citableArgument: Merge TCGA-LUAD mutation data with microbiome 16S/metagenomic profiles. Train combined model. Validate on CheckMate cohort.
ethicalNotes: Microbiome data privacy; consent for stool collection; FDA guidance.

question: Cross-domain: Can a CRISPR screen in patient-derived organoids identify drug-resistance mutations that are invisible in 2D cell line screens?
anchorLabel: CRISPR in PDOs × drug resistance × 3D vs 2D (XD-09)
verdict: 3D organoid CRISPR screens reveal drug-resistance mutations (e.g., in ECM-interaction genes) that 2D screens miss, improving target nomination.
citableArgument: Run matched CRISPR screens in 2D cell lines and 3D patient-derived organoids. Compare resistance mutation profiles. Nominate 3D-specific targets.
ethicalNotes: Patient tissue consent; IACUC for any in vivo follow-up.

question: Cross-domain: Can a digital twin simulation (combining MRI, genomics, and drug PK/PD) predict optimal treatment sequencing for metastatic breast cancer?
anchorLabel: Digital twin × MRI + genomics + PK/PD → treatment sequencing (XD-10)
verdict: A digital twin integrating MRI tumor dynamics, genomic evolution, and drug PK/PD predicts optimal treatment sequencing for metastatic breast cancer, improving PFS.
citableArgument: Build patient-specific digital twin using PhysiCell. Integrate MRI tumor volume, genomic clonal evolution, and drug PK/PD parameters. Simulate treatment sequences. Validate on historical patient data.
ethicalNotes: FDA guidance on digital health; patient data privacy; clinical validation required.
